items.text: SEASON 9 · EPISODE 8 · DRAFT  A meeting room · Solveig, Tamsin, Odile, Raffa, the communications lead, facilities, Maya and Kit · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  A tabletop exercise: the screens say something they shouldn’t, during a full house. Nothing is real — so this is the cheapest place to fail.  ⚑ RV-170 / RV-173: the incident commander decides; everyone else owns a lane. RV-172: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Tabletop
items.stakes: An exercise around a table: the screens say something they shouldn't, during a full house. The point is to fail here, not at the gala.
items.reward: A plan written by role, two people deep — that works with its author out of the room.

objectives.text: Decide what you say at the CEO inject
Find who owns the off switch

items.rumor: The plan's weakest step is the one with your name on it.

items.alt: A meeting room with a whiteboard reading TABLETOP · SCREENS · FULL HOUSE; Solveig at the board; Tamsin and Maya at the table.

bubbles.text: 19:12. The lobby wall shows a false message. Full house. Go.
Tamsin decides. I tell her what's safe to rely on.

items.caption: Nothing here is real. That's the point.

lines.text: Nothing here is real. That's the point. Fail now.
I'm the incident commander. Bring me facts, not opinions.

items.text: Act I — “Nobody owns the off switch”

items.prompt: Inject 4, 19:18: the chief executive phones — “Pull every plug in the building.” What do you say?
unknown: Who can reach the off switch
items.risk: A dark building with no paging — or a lying screen left on.

hints.text: What must stay up — and whose decision is it?

options.label: Back him: pull everything
options.result: Paging and the fire interface go dark with the screens.
options.consequence: Takes down the trusted paths with the untrusted one.
options.fail: The incident commander decides — and never loses paging and life safety.

options.label: Give Tamsin the facts: paging and the fire interface are on their own paths and must stay up; only signage needs to go dark, by facilities at the power controllers or two AV staff in the CMS — her call
options.result: Tamsin: “Signage dark. Paging stays. Tell the chief executive that's my decision.”
options.consequence: Facts to the incident commander; her decision.

options.label: Ignore the chief executive
options.result: He calls again, louder, and nobody has explained anything.

options.label: Go and pull the signage plugs yourself
options.result: Building power is facilities'; the decision is Tamsin's.
options.fail: Power is facilities', on the incident commander's instruction.

items.title: Nobody owns the off switch.
items.body: The screens need to go dark. Facilities hold the signage power controllers; AV holds the rack key; the decision is Tamsin's — and it takes the room ten minutes to agree who does what. The target from detection to paging was 225 seconds. The exercise took 780.
items.label: Test: the extra time — and whose decision it is.

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Solveig and Tamsin beside a board. Detect in sixty seconds, decide in ninety, blank the screens in forty-five, page the house in thirty. Three minutes forty-five. If the person who blanks the screens is at home, it's never. Then the runbook names two people per shift — and neither of them is Maya.

items.title: The runbook assumes Maya.
items.body: Solveig asks Maya to read step 4 of her own runbook aloud. ‘Maya switches signage to safe mode.’ Her mobile number is written next to it. Three nights a week, Maya is at home. On one of them, step 4 is a phone ringing in an empty flat.
items.label: Test: how many people to train — and why roles?

items.prompt: 15:10. Who blanks the screens from now on?
items.risk: A false message left up for ten minutes on the night.
timeout: The gap is still there at the gala.

hints.text: Who decides — and who acts, fast, on every shift?

options.label: Give AV the power-controller key and let them decide
options.result: The decision drifts to whoever holds a key.
options.consequence: Moves a decision to the wrong lane.

options.label: The incident commander decides; facilities cut signage power at the controllers, or two named AV staff blank the CMS — whichever is faster that night — both rehearsed
options.result: Facilities and AV each name two people per shift; Tamsin's card lists both routes.
options.consequence: One decider, two routes, named people.

options.label: A big red button in the lobby
options.result: Anyone can press it — including the next false message's author.

options.label: Whoever's nearest
options.result: Ten minutes of ‘is it me?’ again.

items.title: A war game on a table
items.body: In 1824 a young Prussian officer showed his army's general staff a game played on a table with maps, blocks and dice, where officers made decisions under time pressure and umpires judged the results. The chief of staff is said to have exclaimed that it wasn't a game but training for war. Rehearsing decisions around a table, where mistakes are cheap, spread to armies — and much later to emergency planners.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #89 · AVERY'S LENS  Write the plan by role, not by name  A runbook that names one person fails the night that person is away. Name roles, train two per shift, and rehearse.  Step 4 said ‘Maya switches signage to safe mode’. On the night it matters, Maya is at home.

items.alt: The runbook by role: 0:00 anyone reports to the duty manager; 1:00 the incident commander decides to hold and orders the screens dark; 2:30 facilities cut signage power, or two AV staff blank the CMS; 2:30 security takes the account and keeps the logs; 3:30 the incident commander pages ‘please stay where you are’; 3:30 communications issue a holding statement. Footer: re-run without Maya, 210 s to paging.
items.caption: Written by role, two people deep.

items.title: 780 s
items.body: Solveig's exercise clock: detected 19:12:00, paged 19:25:00 — 780 s. The target was 225 s. Ten minutes of it were four people establishing who could reach the signage power controllers.

items.prompt: Friday. What does the runbook name from now on?
unknown: Who's on shift at the gala
items.risk: A plan that needs its author in the building.

hints.text: Would this plan work if you were on holiday?

options.label: Maya — she's the expert, and on call every night
options.result: One person, every night, for ever.
options.consequence: A single point of failure with a pager.

options.label: Roles, not people: two trained per shift for each AV step, the incident commander's pre-recorded ‘please stay where you are’, and the exercise twice a year with new injects
options.result: Six people trained in two weeks; Tamsin records her message; the next exercise is in the calendar.
options.consequence: The plan works without its author.

options.label: An on-call contractor
options.result: Forty minutes away, on a good night.

items.alt: The meeting room at the re-run; Maya's chair is empty; Kit holds a stopwatch; Tamsin and Solveig.

bubbles.text: Two hundred and ten seconds. Nobody asked for Maya.
That's the best score this exercise can give.

items.prompt: Step four had your name on it. Did you write it that way on purpose?

options.label: “No — I wrote what I'd do. That's the mistake. The plan has to work on the nights I'm not here.”
options.reply: Then train my night duty managers' people. I'll pick the two.

options.label: “It's the safest way.”
options.reply: Not at 23:00 on a Saturday when you're at home.

options.label: “I'll just always be on call.”
options.reply: That's not a plan. That's a burnout date.

items.title: ‘Maya switches signage…’
items.body: The runbook, step 4: ‘Maya switches signage to safe mode.’ Maya wrote it in the second month after opening. It has her mobile number next to it.

items.alt: The meeting room; Odile holds a board paper titled SEASON REVIEW · WHO OWNED WHAT; Maya reads it.

bubbles.text: The board wants a review. Who owned the integrator's accounts? Who approved them? Why did nobody remove them?
The answer's going to be ‘everyone thought someone else did’.

items.caption: Next: *The Review.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  One incident commander decides; security, facilities, communications and AV each own a lane and bring facts. Time the plan (T = Σ stages) and exercise it with injects — the viral video, the executive who wants every plug pulled. Keep paging and life safety up; never counter-message on a lying channel. Write every step by role, train two per shift, and re-run it with the author out of the room.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Which step in your plans only works if you pick up the phone?
